text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 - anomalous routing detected: high error rate and tenant cross-traffic between hosted and dedicated pools. Paging @sre-alex @oncall-ml @eng-runtime. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/routing-anomalies

sre-alex: ack, I'm on. seeing a sharp spike in 5xx from hosted gateway -> dedicated GPUs.

oncall-ml: I'm awake, joining. quick summary?

sre-alex: metrics: hosted requests->dedicated increased ~x12 in 7m. latency +200ms, 5xx from model mismatch (sig mismatch / tokenizer errors). looks like fallback policy sent requests to a dedicated pool configured for a different model variant.

kevin.h: hmm — any tenant overlap reported?

maya: support reporting errors for a handful of customers — 4 customers with garbled outputs (weird tokens), 2 customers seeing 502s. raising impact severity.

nicole: support: customer-facing note drafted: "Investigating intermittent errors affecting some inference requests; engineers triaging."

eng-runtime: throwing in logs from router:
```
2026-03-15T02:11:12Z router INFO route_request tenant=acme region=us-east intended_pool=hosted fallback_pool=dedicated-ml-1 model_variant=redwood-7b-q8
2026-03-15T02:11:12Z router WARN routing_policy: capacity_tier_blend=true override_isolate_tenants=false
2026-03-15T02:11:12Z dedicated-ml-1 ERROR model_load_mismatch expected_variant=redwood-7b-q8 actual_variant=redwood-13b-fp16
2026-03-15T02:11:12Z request ERROR tokenization_failed tenant=acme
```
\neng-runtime: so dedicated pool has 13b fp16 pinned; router thought it could route redwood-7b-q8 requests there (quant mismatch) because policy allows variant fallback.

platformd: also seeing region fallback loop between us-east and us-west. policy has region_fallback: true and both regions have different model inventories; requests flip-flop when dedicated pool responds with mismatch -> router sends to next region -> next region does same -> back to original region. loop causes retries and amplifies load.

oncall-ml: immediate mitigation suggestions?

sre-alex: mitigation plan (short):
1) temporarily disable capacity-tier blend for hosted->dedicated: `PATCH /admin/policies/routing {"capacity_tier_blend": false}`
2) set `isolate_tenants=true` so dedicated pools won't accept hosted tenant traffic: `PATCH /admin/pools/dedicated-ml-1 {"isolate_tenants": true}`
3) throttle retries / enable circuit-breaker for cross-region fallbacks: `PATCH /admin/policies/retries {"max_attempts":1}`
4) notify support and run cleanup job for affected requests.

kevin.h: I'll run step 1 and 2 now.

ops-bot: deploy started by kevin.h: PATCH /admin/policies/routing id=policy-93 request_id=slack-1773456789

kevin.h: done for step 1 and 2. responses look green on config API.

ops-bot: config apply ok (ea5f3c). Propagating to routers.

sre-alex: monitoring... 3m after change: host->dedicated traffic dropped to baseline, 5xxs trending down. region fallback loop count decreased to 0.

oncall-ml: good. I'm taking the incident for next 45m to validate no regressions, will hand off to eng-runtime after.

maya: support update sent to customers. advising they may see improved behavior.

eng-runtime: follow-up: we should add a safety check to routing engine: verify target pool model_variant compatibility before sending request. quick patch suggestion: if !compatible && fallback_pool_is_dedicated then skip and failover to local degrade variant.

sre-alex: can we add guard in config: `prevent_variant_promotion=true`?

platformd: raising an EPIC to track long-term fixes: validation, better metrics, and a routing circuit-breaker mechanism. ticket: INF-3482.

nicole: support: list of affected tenants: acme, beta-co, finx, zeta-app. all contacted.

eng-runtime: root cause hypothesis: a recent routing policy change (PR #4521) enabled `capacity_tier_blend` with default override flags; that PR assumed model parity across pools which is not true for dedicated pools managed by customers. the policy allowed hosted requests to fall back into dedicated pools without tenant isolation or variant checks. combined with region_fallback retries caused the loop.

kevin.h: saved a snapshot of current policy and reverted the risky defaults. will follow up PR to add compatibility checks in the router.

sre-alex: next actions:
- oncall-ml to monitor for 2h and escalate if error rate resurges
- eng-runtime to implement variant compatibility short-circuit (patch + canary)
- platform to update runbook with explicit guidance about `capacity_tier_blend` and `isolate_tenants` defaults
- postmortem draft (owner: sre-alex) within 48h

oncall-ml: acknowledged. I'll collect metric dashboards and attach to postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> partial. P0 -> P1.

sre-alex: moving to tracking channel for post-incident work. will close this thread after handoff. thanks all. :thumbsup:

platformd: created INF-3482 and linked PRs: https://redwood/INF-3482

eng-runtime: reminder: please review dedicated pool onboarding checklist — ensure model inventory tags match expected serving variants.

nicole: support will follow up with impacted customers with timeline and next steps.

sre-alex: last check 45m after mitigation: error rate back to baseline, no further tenant cross-traffic observed. closing page in 15m unless someone objects.

maya: no objections, thanks team.

sre-alex: closing thread.
